transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Student health sent me because they said my weight is too low to clear me for the youth workshops. The number has kept going down, apparently, but I mean... when I’m busy and focused, that just kind of happens.
When you notice your weight going down, how do you feel about it—do you find yourself trying to avoid gaining weight, or is this happening without you really trying to lose weight at all?
I do try to avoid gaining. Even thinking about gaining a pound makes me panic. If I eat a normal dinner, or something with butter, I feel like everyone will be able to tell I’ve lost discipline.
When you look at yourself now, even at this lower weight, do you see or feel like you're still too heavy or not thin enough?
Yeah. I mean, in photos from the showcase, I don’t really look at the artwork first. I zoom in on my arms and my waist. If I look small enough, I feel like I’m being serious and put-together.
Have you ever had episodes where you eat a large amount of food and feel out of control, followed by things like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising intensely to make up for it?
No, I haven’t had episodes like that.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, and do you know what your BMI or weight percentile has been calculated at?

I don’t know my BMI or percentile. Student health just told me my weight was too low to clear me for the youth workshops, and that it’s kept dropping. But honestly, it feels like I’ve just been focused and busy.
Can you tell me your current height and weight in numbers, even approximately, so I can calculate your BMI?
I don’t really know the number, sorry. Student health just said it was too low to clear me for the youth workshops, and that it’s been dropping. I’ve mostly felt like I’m just busy and focused.
Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual periods, like them becoming irregular or stopping altogether, since your weight has been going down?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been paying close attention to my periods lately.
Do you happen to remember what your weight was at your last check-up or clinic visit, even roughly, in pounds or kilograms?
I don’t remember the actual number. They just told me it had gone down again and was too low for them to clear me for the workshops. I guess I haven’t really tracked it—I’ve just been busy.
Have you noticed things like feeling unusually cold, your hair thinning, dizziness, or fainting spells lately?
I’m not sure about those things. Student health was mostly concerned that my weight keeps dropping and is too low for the workshops, but I’ve just felt like I’ve been focused and busy.
Would you be willing to have your height and weight measured here today so we can get an accurate number to work with?
I guess so. Student health keeps saying my weight is too low and that it’s been dropping, even though it just feels like I’ve been focused and busy.
How long has this pattern of eating less and losing weight been going on—weeks, months, or longer?

It’s been going on for a while—months, I think. I kind of plan my day around not eating much: coffee before studio, maybe a few bites from the café if people are watching. I avoid bread or anything oily because it feels like that would undo the control I’ve worked for.
Let's go ahead and measure your height and weight right now on the scale here—can you step on so we can get those exact numbers?

Okay. I know student health has been worried because the number keeps going down and they say it’s too low for me to be cleared for the workshops, even though I don’t really feel like I’m doing anything extreme.
Can you tell me whether your periods have stopped completely for the last few months, even if you haven't been tracking them closely?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping track of them closely.
Now that you're on the scale, can you tell me exactly what your height and weight read?
I… I can see it’s lower again. Student health keeps saying it’s too low for them to clear me for the youth workshops, but I don’t know—it feels like I’ve just been busy and focused.
Looking at the display right now, what are the exact numbers for your height and weight?
I can see it’s gone down again. I don’t really know the exact numbers—I just know student health says it’s too low for me to be cleared for the youth workshops.
Since you're already on the scale, would it be okay if I read the exact height and weight numbers directly from the display myself?
Yeah, that’s okay. Student health has been worried because the number keeps dropping and they say it’s too low for the workshops, even though I just feel like I’ve been busy and focused.
I'm looking at the display now—it shows your height as [X] and weight as [Y]. Can you confirm you're comfortable with me recording these exact numbers in your chart?

Yes, you can record them. Student health sent me because they keep saying my weight is too low for the youth workshops, and it has been dropping. I mean, I’ve just been really focused and busy, but… okay.
Have your menstrual periods stopped completely for three months or more in a row?
I'm not really sure—I haven't been keeping track closely.
Would it be okay if I contacted student health directly to get the exact height and weight numbers they recorded, so I can calculate your BMI precisely?
Yeah, that’s okay. Student health has the numbers—they’ve been concerned because my weight keeps dropping and they say it’s too low for the workshops.
Now that we have your height and weight recorded, can you tell me roughly how many pounds or kilograms you’ve lost in total over the past few months?

I don’t know the total amount exactly. Student health just keeps saying the number has been dropping and that it’s too low for me to be cleared for the workshops. I guess I haven’t really been paying attention to the pounds—I’ve just been focused and busy.
